Is this the beginning of a sustainable post-election rally into Christmas, or just another bull trap?

Sometimes markets test the 200-day, experience distribution, and then reclaim it. If that reclaim holds, it could signal a meaningful improvement in the trend.

posts.name: Spencer Pratt
posts.text:
We're in a new era of communication, and only one side seems to be living in it. The old guard consultant class is about to be relegated to the dustbin of history. 

If you think that high prices lost the election for the right, you don't understand marketing. Humans have no problem paying a premium for a good quality brand. Notice the word "brand", not "product". Are Nikes better than New Balance? Nope. But the brand is better. And notice what happened when they tinkered with the brand and screwed their core narrative? Nike stock fell through the basement. Did the product change? Nope. The brand did.  

It's not the product, it's the brand. Results don't sell the product, the storytelling does. Will these newly-elected commies lower prices? Of course not. Are they gonna get you free healthcare? No, your insurance is gonna get even worse, just like it did the last time they tried socialized medicine. They're not going to do anything they've sold you, but...like Saul Goodman said: if you're committed enough, you can make any story work.

The committed storytelling of a couple insane podcasters was enough to fracture an entire political coalition from their own side in less than 2 years...they have zero power, zero credibility, they've never actually governed anything nor produced any results, but...they're good storytellers, and that's all that matters. Are they telling a good story? No, it's atrocious, but they're telling their atrocious story effectively and compellingly. 

It is 100% true that everything's too damn expensive, and we all know that inflated prices are always sticky. Does anyone know that it's entirely the result of shutting down the global economy over the flu and (both naive republicans and democrats) printing infinity dollars for several years? Nope...because nobody has effectively told that story, and it's an unsexy story to tell. "Free stuff!" is a VERY easy story to tell, and when everyone's gotta take out a second mortgage just to pay their insurance premiums, "free healthcare" is an unbeatable story. It doesn't matter that "free healthcare" doesn't exist and socialized medicine is a terrible product...it's not the product, it's the brand. And "FREE!" is a great brand.

You can't get mad at people for having the financial literacy of a 9 year old. I mean, you can, but they outnumber you a million to one, so it's not going to be productive. You need to figure out how to make an unsexy story sexy, or else the "free stuff!" crowd is going to eat your lunch every time. If you give people a choice between earning a six pack on a treadmill or taking Ozempic, they're gonna choose Ozempic...they don't care about the side effects. If you give people a choice between fiscal discipline or free stuff...guess what they'll pick? They don't care about the side effects. 

With projected growth of 5%, the economy right now is stronger than it's been in generations. Is that the story you hear? Nope. Is that the vibe you feel? Absolutely not, especially when every time you fill up your gas tank, it feels like a diesel enema. 

It's not the product, it's the brand. A great product can fall into oblivion with bad messaging...a single bad review from one effective storyteller can tank a restaurant. The "influencer economy" is lucrative for a reason; everybody inherently understands the importance of effective storytelling...except the right. Zohran Mamdani gets it...he has an army of influencers on staff. In a perfect metaphor of this transitional phase of old guard vs new wave political messaging, Zohran nuked the Vice President into oblivion with maybe the biggest ratio in the history of the internet. By simply posting the subway assistant meme, Mamdani got 2 MILLION likes, quoting a post from the VP that had only 10K likes. If you're reading that sentence thinking "this is fucking ridiculous, you're talking about social media likes as political analysis now?"...you are the problem. 

Yes, this stuff matters. Rizz matters.

20.000 euro!

Dat is wat iemand die 100.000 euro op een spaarrekening bij de grootbanken had gezet sinds 2020 aan koopkracht heeft verloren. 20% van je koopkracht zomaar verdwenen.

De reden is simpel. In Nederland is de rente zo laag dat je met ‘veilig’ sparen niet eens in de buurt komt van het tempo waarmee het dagelijkse leven elk jaar duurder wordt.

Sinds 2020 ligt de inflatie gemiddeld op net geen 4% (3,9% om precies te zijn). Schrik niet: volgens De Nederlandsche Bank lag de spaarrente over dezelfde periode op 0,7%. Geen wonder dat de koopkracht van ons spaargeld zo extreem hard is gedaald.

Zelfs als je bij andere banken gemiddeld een procentpunt meer rente had gekregen, is de koopkracht van die 100.000 euro sinds 2020 nog steeds met meer dan 15% gedaald.

Ik neem die 100.000 euro omdat dit het maximale bedrag is dat, op papier, per persoon, per bank wordt beschermd via het depositogarantiestelsel. Daar zit naar schatting nu zo’n 5 miljard euro in. Dat bedrag kan, wederom op papier, worden vergroot. Mocht zich een systeemcrisis voordoen, waarbij meerdere banken omvallen, dan is de kans groot dat slechts een deel van die 100.000 euro wordt vergoed.

Immers, het totale Nederlandse spaargeld bedraagt momenteel liefst 666 miljard euro (een ironisch getal). Mijn schatting is dat de koopkracht van al het Nederlandse spaargeld sinds 2020 met grofweg 100 miljard euro is afgenomen.

Laat dat even rustig op je inwerken. En weet je wat het bizarre is? Zelfs als maar de helft van ons spaargeld (je hebt nu eenmaal een potje nodig voor als het even tegenzit) de voorbije jaren slim was belegd, dan zaten Nederlanders er nog een heel, heel stuk warmer bij.

Dat betekent dus weg van sparen, maar ook van obligaties naar bijvoorbeeld aandelen. Denk bovendien aan alternatieve beleggingen zoals goud, bitcoin of wellicht vastgoed. Heel veel beleggingen hebben beter gepresteerd dan sparen en obligaties.

Saillant detail gezien alle discussies in de politiek: de belasting op vermogen, vooral via box 3, zou enorm veel hoger zijn geweest, terwijl Nederlanders er gemiddeld (altijd gemiddeld) flink op vooruit waren gegaan.

Onlangs schreef ik nog maar eens een artikel over hoe Nederlanders omgaan met hun vermogen, vaak verdiend door gewoon hard te werken. Daar zit heel veel ruimte voor verbetering. Zoals deze grafiek nog maar eens laat zien: sparen is helaas geen deugd.

Je vindt de link in de comments. Vergeet niet je meteen in te schrijven, het is gratis.

Looking at the data on this election and my view has changed a bit. 

Looking at the deep red state senate wins like Texas and SC and the result has mostly a story of insane voter turnout for Dems. 

Democratic vote counts were almost in line with the 2024 presidential election. Republican votes dipped off like they do in most midterms. Some of this does reflect a shift in voter party preference (more in TX than SC where they elected a Republican governor) but I think it was mostly Democrats capitalizing on their broad based hatred of Trump to drive voters to the polls (black voters, women, extremely liberal bloc [trans/LGBTQ issues], Hispanics [scared of ICE]).
